observation: The 3-round architecture-critique loop caught a live, ship-blocking bug before any code was written: round 2 flagged that the planner's locked template-read redesign (naive `${role}.md` + `^[a-z][a-z-]*$` regex) would 404 the `product_manager` and `qa_engineer` agent-template routes, which `AgentEditor.tsx` and `AgentAddDialog.tsx` call live from the web UI, because the real seeded filenames are hyphenated (`product-manager.md`) while the role names use underscores. Round 3's map-as-allowlist fix (reusing factory-bootstrap's explicit role->filename array) closed both the regression and the traversal risk. This validates the cost of the critique loop.

The WP spec (TRACK-AU.md AU18) named exactly 8 files as factorySettings' full call-site surface, despite its own 'Plan calls' section explicitly warning in advance that AU12 and AU13 both undercounted scope by roughly 3-7x on first audit and to 'budget accordingly.' The planner's own round-1 architecture pass still only reached 16 files (server+db) -- already 2x the spec's estimate -- and still completely missed packages/eval (an entire package with its own generic KV writer, seedFactorySettings, used at 8+ call sites), bringing the true count to ~21 files across 3 packages once round-1 critique caught the eval blind spot. Even an explicit advance warning citing the exact historical multiplier did not prevent a fresh undercount.

packages/eval was entirely absent from both the WP spec's own scope description and the planner's first-round architecture pass, despite packages/eval being a real tsconfig project reference that imports factorySettings via the db barrel. It was caught only by the reviewer's independent re-verification in round-1 architecture-critique. Had it not been caught, AC-4's verification method (git grep factorySettings scoped to packages/server/src + packages/db/src only) would have returned green while packages/eval's compile was actually broken by the barrel drop -- a false-green on a graded acceptance criterion.

The two-sub-phase builder split (Half B factorySettings retirement landed first across 3 commits, then Half A notificationQueue ownership landed second in 1 commit) worked cleanly per the plan's own B-first sequencing recommendation: zero merge conflicts, each sub-phase independently verified green (full npm run verify, including both new lint-chain guards) before the next started, confirmed by the commit history and review.md's methodology section.

The Phase 4 code review found only 1 non-blocking WARNING (stale docs, correctly triaged to the separate write-docs cadence) and 0 CRITICAL across a ~30-file, 13-commit diff. review.md's own methodology shows this reflects real independent verification rather than under-scrutiny: the reviewer re-ran every gate itself (check 10/10 packages, lint, test 436 pass, test:integration:service 2737 pass/0 fail, both new guards' --fixtures AND --check), independently re-confirmed headline claims against the diff (e.g., the '18 exported functions' claim resolved to 16 production + 2 test-support, verified by reading the module header and grep), and scrutinized all 3 builder-flagged deviations individually rather than trusting the builder's self-report. The low defect count plausibly reflects the 3-round architecture hardening paying off in fewer code-level surprises.

Round-3 architecture-critique's own SUGGESTION section asserted 'seedAgent already exposes an optional costActualMinor opt (packages/eval/src/seeding.ts:155/:172, defaulting to null)' as a verified-against-code fact. Git history shows this field did not exist on origin/main -- the builder had to add it as a new opt in commit 1f83438f ('adds an optional costActualMinor to seedAgent'). This is a factual error in a critique round that explicitly prided itself on verifying every claim against source rather than trusting narrative (round 1's whole premise). The builder silently corrected it rather than the error being caught by the critique process itself.

While rewriting the eval graded cost-sentinel scenarios, the builder hit a pre-existing, unrelated FK mismatch bug in the eval CLI run: seedTeam's default id is a random UUID while seedBuiltinRoutines hardcodes 'prod-1', reproduced identically on origin/main before this WP's changes. Correctly identified as out-of-scope and not fixed (documented in commit 1f83438f's body and flagged in the builder report), but this is a real latent bug in shared eval-seeding infrastructure now surfaced for a future work package to pick up.

review.md's Adversarial/Simplification lens individually scrutinized all 3 builder deviations from the plan's named 18 repository functions and judged each justified rather than drift: (a) findById/listAll test-support reads were necessary because the zero-allowlist guard forbids tests touching the table directly, so generic assertions needed repository-mediated reads -- test-only, documented in the module header; (b) a dead QueueStatus type deletion was zero-orphan-ref clean; (c) limit params on listByStatus/listUnread were behavior-preserving carryovers of pre-existing route-level .limit() calls, not speculative additions. This reads as healthy, well-bounded builder discretion within a well-specified plan rather than a sign of plan under-specification -- the deviations were narrow, individually justifiable, and independently re-verified by the reviewer rather than rubber-stamped.

Docs staleness caused by this WP's schema changes (factory_settings table drop, cost_actual write removal, template storage move) was caught and precisely enumerated by the code reviewer -- 6 specific doc locations across 5 files with exact line numbers -- rather than either being silently missed or incorrectly blocking the WP verdict. The plan had explicitly scoped zero doc changes into its own file table, and the reviewer correctly triaged this to the separate write-docs cadence as a single non-blocking WARNING instead of inventing scope.

The recurring 'work-package spec undercounts real codebase call-site scope' pattern (documented explicitly in this WP's own spec text as an AU12/AU13 precedent, and reconfirmed here on AU18 -- 3 distinct work packages now) has no corresponding row in .pipeline/compound-candidates.md (rows C1-C6 cover integration-proof gaps, scope-creep-beyond-plan, lint-skipping, stale-base drift, critique fact-audits, and infra overhead, but none cover scope-undercount-within-a-spec). This looks like a 3-occurrence pattern that should qualify for compound-candidate tracking (EMERGING/CONFIRMED) but has not yet been promoted -- worth surfacing to the next /pipeline:compound run.
